answer.evidence: The object is a two-tier open rack. The top cap is rows 2-4: two light rows (L about 150-170) and a lighter edge line at row 4 (#afb1b8). Darker rows 5-13 below it (L about 114) act as shadow and back wall. The middle shelf at rows 15-17 repeats the pattern: two light rows, an edge line at row 17, then darker rows 18-19. The base at rows 27-29 does the same, with an edge line at row 29. These stacked shelf surfaces and the magazine contents show a top view plus a front face about 26 rows tall. The top cap is only 3 rows, which is borderline, but it has a clear edge line and shadow. The silhouette also widens downward from 20 to 30 px, which suggests a stepped, receding form.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small magazine rack: a blue-grey cabinet with a lighter top edge, shelf shading and a few magazines in red, green and yellow. It shows about 5 lightness steps on the cabinet body, with a highlight edge, mid tone and dark base. Its outline leans visibly blue-grey, and the measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so it is not a black sticker line. Forms are separated partly by value alone. There are no large flat fills (near-flat coverage 0%). It carries 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which is above prop-hedge (9) and below prop-stall-cheese (17) and prop-well-roofed (20). Texture is moderate: the magazine covers and shelf edges have small variations, but there is less grain than on the stall or well. It is roughly equal to the mid-range references and would sit acceptably next to them, though slightly simpler than the richest ones.

The same pattern repeats at rows 15-17, where a second shelf band has an edge line at row 17 and a dark shadow at rows 18-20. So each tier shows a horizontal surface. The front face of the whole piece runs about rows 5-30, which is well over 3 rows. The top band is only about 3 rows, which is thin but has an edge line and shadow, so it counts as a top surface and not a bare rim. The magazines are goods on shelves and are counted as decor.
